cause: The edit is effectively the last step, so the provided tests are almost never run afterwards. Failures a single test run would expose (an unhandled error path, a missing attribute, an unimplemented function) go to grading unverified; it should always reserve a step to run the tests and fix what fails.
subject: Re-runs the tests after an edit, before the next model call.
description: The agent loop now remembers the last test command the model ran (any bash call matching the existing `TEST_COMMAND` set). After a reply that changes files, if the model didn't already run the tests after that change, the loop runs that same command again itself and appends its output to the changed file's tool result (`retestChange` in `src/agent.ts`). The command is re-run as the model ran it — same cwd, sandbox and signal — and only when a step remains, so a failing run lands in front of the model while the step that would otherwise be its final answer can fix it. This costs a command and some tokens, not an extra model call, and it guarantees the change is checked rather than sent to grading unverified. In my temporary test the loop re-ran the tests and put the output with the edit, skipped when the model had already re-run them after the edit, did nothing with no test command, and did nothing on the last step. The full suite shows the same 195 pass / 11 fail (the sandbox/ps failures) before and after.

verdict.reason: no better on the training tasks (+5 points, ahead in 63% of resamples, cost ×1.19)
